Error

Errors in python can be distinguished in two different
kinds: syntax errors and exceptions.
Syntax errors are the most common kind of error we get while
learning Python.
>>>for iin range(5): print('Hello world’)
>>>SyntaxError: invalid syntax

Exceptions

A program may be syntactically correct, but it may cause an
error during execution.
Errors detected during execution are called exceptions.
An exception is an event that disrupts the normal flow of the
program's instructions.
When a Python script encounters a situation that it can't
handle, it raises an exception.

Exceptions
An exception is a Python object that represents an error.
When a Python script raises an exception, it must be
handled immediately otherwise it would terminate and
come out.

Example
A = list(range(10))
o_count=0
e_count=0
for i in range(20):
if A[i]%2==0:
e_count+=1
else:
o_count+=1
print("Count of even numbers: ",e_count)
print("Count of odd numbers: ",o_count)
Without 
Exception 
Handling
IndexError: list index out of range

Example
A = list(range(10))
o_count=0
e_count=0
for i in range(20):
try:
if A[i]%2==0:
e_count+=1
else:
o_count+=1
except:
print("Index out of range")
break
print("Count of even numbers: ",e_count)
print("Count of odd numbers: ",o_count)
With 
Exception 
Handling

Handling an exception
• The try-finally clause:
•You can use a finally: block along with a try: block.
try:
You do your operations here;
......................
Due to any exception, this may be skipped.  
finally:
This would always be executed.
......................

Handling an exception
• The try-finally clause: Example
try:
fh = open("testfile", "w")
fh.write("This is my test file for exception handling!!")
finally:
fh.close()

Handling an exception
• Try: This block will test the excepted error to occur
• Except: Here you can handle the error
• Else: If there is no exception then this block will be executed
• Finally: Finally block always gets executed either exception is generated 
or not
• Syntax:
try:
# Some Code… 
except:
# Optional block
# Exception Handling  (if required)
else:
# Execute if no exception occurs
finally:
# Some code .....(always executed)
